News & Analysis on Domestic and International Trade, National and State Finances, Budget, Government Regulation, Monetary Policy, RBI Rates, Interest Rates, CRR, Indian Trade, Monetary and Industrial Policy.

item.title: India on track to hit $1 trillion exports target in FY27: Commerce Secretary
item.description: India's exports increased by 16.6% in the first half of this fiscal year. The country aims to reach $1 trillion in exports by 2026-27. Commerce Secretary Rajesh Agrawal stated that India is on track to meet this goal. Despite global trade uncertainties, India continues to be viewed positively as a trusted trading partner. India achieved record exports of $863 billion in the previous fiscal year.

item.title: India, US close to finalising trade deal talks, signing may take time
item.description: The trade deal negotiations between India and the US are nearing completion, according to Commerce Secretary Rajesh Agrawal. He stated that the legal texts are almost finalized. However, the signing hinges on the establishment of new US tariff rules and the resolution of ongoing Section 301 investigations.

item.title: RBI may hike interest rates by 75 basis points by Q2 of next year: Goldman Sachs
item.description: The Reserve Bank of India is projected to increase interest rates by 75 basis points by the second quarter of 2027. Analysts predict that headline inflation will remain above 6 percent into early 2027 before gradually decreasing. Despite the monetary tightening, India's GDP growth is expected to moderate to 7.2 percent in 2027. Strong domestic demand and an emerging investment cycle are likely to sustain economic activity.

item.title: Onion farmers seek measures to ensure Rs 3,000 per quintal amid surplus production outlook
item.description: Maharashtra onion farmers have asked the Centre to ensure prices of at least Rs 3,000 per quintal by expanding export markets and maintaining a stable export policy, as India is expected to have a sizeable surplus in 2025-26. The growers’ body said better export infrastructure, storage, processing and transparent supply data will be critical to prevent price crashes when market arrivals rise.

item.title: Govt planning to expand AB-PMJAY packages for public hospitals from 23 to 112: NHA sources
item.description: The National Health Authority has proposed expanding health benefit packages reserved for government hospitals under Ayushman Bharat from 23 to 112, adding 89 treatments and procedures. The move aims to improve access to healthcare closer to beneficiaries' homes and channel more reimbursements into strengthening public hospital infrastructure and services.

item.title: Indian economic growth seen at annual 7.6% in July-September quarter, economists say
item.description: India's economy is predicted to grow by 7.6% in the July-September quarter according to economists. Consumer demand has shown resilience, mitigating the effects of rising inflation pressures. Predictions indicate continued strength from passenger vehicle sales and bank credit growth. Despite potential slowdowns in the second half of the fiscal year, investments are expected to improve. The Reserve Bank of India may raise rates as economic conditions evolve.

item.title: How India became a rice powerhouse - and why it's becoming a problem
item.description: India's rice production has significantly increased, bolstered by government subsidies and new crop varieties. This rise in output has led to a surplus that threatens fiscal stability due to high subsidy costs. Political tensions arise between the central and state governments regarding rice pricing and production. While domestic demand is not expected to grow significantly, exports continue to increase.

item.title: Nitin Gadkari approves road projects worth Rs 1,123 crore on Delhi-Agra corridor, Rs 359 crore for West Delhi road
item.description: The project, covering National Highways 44 and 19, aims to improve connectivity and traffic efficiency along the corridor, which handles approximately 68,000 passenger car units (PCUs) daily, including freight, industrial, commuter and tourist traffic.

item.title: States' subsidy, cash transfer outgo jumps from 16% to 21% of revenue receipts in 5 years: Report
item.description: States' spending on subsidies and transfers has risen significantly over recent years and is expected to continue growing. By 2026-27, states are estimated to spend around 1 percent of GDP on cash transfer schemes. Major contributors to this increase are power subsidies and unconditional transfers for various beneficiaries, including women and farmers. States such as Andhra Pradesh and Chhattisgarh are among the highest spenders in these categories.

item.title: India, Philippines discuss defence, trade ties as PM Modi meets President Marcos Jr.
item.description: Prime Minister Narendra Modi and President Ferdinand R. Marcos Jr. discussed enhancing cooperation in various sectors. They acknowledged the momentum in bilateral relations, particularly in defence and investment areas. The two leaders reflected on their previous meetings, emphasising the importance of their strategic partnership. India aims to expand its engagement with Southeast Asian nations through diverse initiatives.

item.title: India's GDP growth pegged at 7.3% in FY26-27, may touch 7.7% next quarter: EAC-PM Chairman
item.description: India's GDP is expected to grow by 7.3% this financial year and 7.7% in the next quarter, S Mahendra Dev, Chairman of EAC-PM said. Sustained export momentum and improving foreign investment are crucial for this growth, he added.

item.title: Budget 2027: FM Sitharaman chairs third pre-Budget consultation with manufacturing sector leaders
item.description: Nirmala Sitharaman chaired the third pre-Budget consultation meeting for the Union Budget 2027-28 in New Delhi. The meeting included representatives from the manufacturing sector and senior government officials providing suggestions. This exercise aims to gather inputs from various economic sectors to shape the Budget's priorities. The Union Budget is scheduled for presentation on February 1, 2027, along with the Economic Survey.

item.title: Odisha govt hikes Dearness Allowance by 3% for state employees
item.description: Odisha Chief Minister Mohan Charan Majhi announced a three percent hike in Dearness Allowance for government employees. The increase raises the DA from 60 percent to 63 percent, effective from July 1. Pensioners will also benefit from the same three percent increase in Dearness Relief. Approximately 8.5 lakh government employees and pensioners will receive this additional financial support. Payments reflecting the increased DA will be included in the November salary.

item.title: India's CAD may touch 1.2% of GDP in FY27 as oil, gold demand pose risks: UBI
item.description: India's current account deficit is projected to reach 1.2% of GDP in FY27, driven by oil prices, according to a report by Union Bank of India. The report emphasizes that high crude oil prices and gold demand could impact the external balance. Merchandise trade deficit widened to a significant USD 39.88 billion in October. Additionally, imports surged while services trade surplus remained nearly flat during the same period.

item.title: Inflation Crosses 6%: Did RBI Act Too Late? | The Morning Brief Decode
India Inc.’s sudden craving for dollars is a dangerous gamble
item.description: India's increasing reliance on US dollar borrowing poses potential risks for future financial stability and currency strength. The Reserve Bank of India has promoted overseas dollar raising, but this could lead to vulnerabilities. Strengthening dollar reserves through debt might not address underlying economic issues effectively.

item.title: Wholesale inflation faces a triple squeeze from fuel, food and metals in FY27: Report
item.description: India's wholesale inflation is currently anticipated to reach around 11 percent in FY27, surpassing earlier projections. Persistent pressures from energy and input costs alongside risks to food prices are significant factors. The report highlights that global commodity prices will greatly influence this inflation trajectory. A potential 25-basis-point rate hike by the Reserve Bank of India is also expected in December.

item.title: Egypt, India aim to hit $12 bn bilateral trade target within five years, says Foreign Minister Badr Abdelatty
item.description: Egypt and India are aiming to increase bilateral trade to $12 billion over the next five years and expand Indian investment in the North African country, Egyptian Foreign Minister Badr Abdelatty said. The target was discussed during Commerce Minister Piyush Goyal's visit to Egypt with an Indian business delegation.

item.title: India's economic strength underpins attractive investment climate: Nirmala Sitharaman
item.description: "The USISPF Board reiterated its commitment to investing in India, including in R&D, reflecting confidence in India's growth story and innovation ecosystem," the Finance Ministry said in a post on X.

item.title: India-EU should ensure maximum utilisation of FTA: Ambassador Jean-Eric Paquet
item.description: The agreement will not only ensure that trade flourishes but also will open new opportunities, including those in research and innovation, with Assam poised to benefit from it, he said.

item.title: India's sugar output more than doubles to 23.59 lakh tonnes by November 15
item.description: India has seen a significant rise in sugar production, reaching 23.59 lakh tonnes by November 15. This increase is attributed mainly to the early start of crushing operations in Maharashtra. Sugar mills in Maharashtra rose to 154, contributing 18.51 lakh tonnes of sugar production. Other states like Uttar Pradesh and Karnataka are gradually boosting their crushing activities.

item.title: India's 2025-26 edible oil import bill up 24 pc to record Rs 2 lakh cr; crude palm oil buying surges
item.description: Edible oil imports in the 2025-26 oil year (November-October) increased compared with 16.01 million tonnes a year earlier, when the bill was about Rs 161,126 crore, the trade body said in a statement.

item.title: India’s unemployment rate eases to 4.9% in October
item.description: India’s unemployment rate for those aged 15 and above declined to 4.9% in October from 5% in September, government data showed, below the 5.1% forecast in a Reuters poll.

item.title: LTCG tax relief on the cards? CBDT Chairman says govt examining proposals for equity capital gains tax changes before Union Budget
item.description: CBDT Chairman Ravi Agrawal said that the government is evaluating industry suggestions for LTCG and STT taxes. Pre-Budget meetings are ongoing with various stakeholders contributing their proposals for consideration. The government aims to enhance ease of doing business through effective policy decisions based on stakeholder feedback. Agrawal reported an increase in direct tax collections and substantial refunds issued this fiscal year.

item.title: India, US have resolved bulk of trade deal issues, pact could be sealed soon: Jaishankar
item.description: India and the US have nearly resolved issues regarding the proposed trade deal. External Affairs Minister S Jaishankar expressed hope that the agreement could soon be finalized. Negotiations have focused primarily on changes needed from the American side. The upcoming meeting between Prime Minister Narendra Modi and President Trump may further progress the deal. Securing this trade pact would significantly benefit India’s economy in the large context.

item.title: India's consumption story remains strong, but rural demand faces inflation risks: Report
item.description: India's consumption growth is projected to be robust, driven by a young population and digital adoption. Despite this, rural income pressures and food inflation could pose challenges for near-term demand. Premium products are expected to outperform mass-market categories as consumer preferences evolve. The impact of Super El Nino may exacerbate rural demand issues due to agricultural pressures. Companies must adapt to changing consumer dynamics and enhance operational efficiencies for success.

item.title: FICCI calls for comprehensive India-Africa trade framework
item.description: India and Africa are encouraged to develop a comprehensive trade arrangement to enhance economic cooperation. Ficci emphasizes the importance of a predictable framework to address trade barriers and promote investment. With the upcoming visit of Commerce Minister Piyush Goyal to Egypt, both regions aim to strengthen ties. Egypt's strategic location provides opportunities for Indian companies in various sectors.

item.title: Five sectors account for 83% of India's record October merchandise export surge: Report
item.description: Exports from the five sectors - engineering goods, petroleum products, electronic goods, gems and jewellery, and organic and inorganic chemicals - increased 59.4 per cent to USD 34.37 billion in October, compared with USD 21.56 billion in the corresponding month last year.

item.title: Tamil Nadu govt imposes stock limits on paddy, rice and pulses amid price rise
item.description: The Tamil Nadu government has set stock limits on essential commodities like rice and pulses to combat price inflation. Wholesalers can stock a maximum of 2,000 metric tonnes of rice, while retailers are restricted to eight tonnes. Miller stock is limited to one month's production capacity, ensuring regular supply. Importers are prohibited from holding stock longer than 45 days post customs clearance, promoting quick turnover.

item.title: India achieves historic $90 billion export milestone in October: Piyush Goyal at IITF inauguration
RBI imposes monetary penalty on One Mobikwik Systems
item.description: In a release, the central bank said a statutory inspection of the company was conducted by the RBI with reference to its operations for the period from June 2025 to March 2026.

item.title: US assures India lower tariffs than peers in trade deal
item.description: The US has assured India of lower tariffs than those imposed on its trading partners under the proposed trade deal. The first phase of the agreement will cover goods, with services to be negotiated separately in the next phase.

item.title: India's gold imports plunge 62.57% to $5.51 billion in October as prices fall below $4,000/oz
item.description: India's gold imports fell 39.9% to $24.78 billion during April-October 2026, down from $41.24 billion a year ago, according to Commerce Ministry data. October imports plunged 62.57% year-on-year to $5.51 billion amid a correction in global gold prices. Meanwhile, India's gems and jewellery exports rose to $18.50 billion during the seven-month period.

item.title: Supply shocks to weaken monetary policy effectiveness: CEA
item.description: Chief Economic Advisor V Anantha Nageswaran emphasized the diminishing effectiveness of interest rate adjustments in controlling inflation due to supply chain disruptions. He indicated that fiscal policies will play a critical role in addressing these supply-induced challenges. Nageswaran highlighted that many countries have struggled to meet their inflation targets since 2022. He underscored the potential long-term dominance of supply shocks in inflation dynamics.

item.title: Food inflation to stay elevated; ICICI Bank sees 25 bps RBI rate hike in December
item.description: Food inflation in India is projected to remain elevated in the coming months due to a shortfall in crops. The Reserve Bank of India is anticipated to raise interest rates by 25 basis points to manage retail inflation. Factors such as weak monsoon and high energy prices contribute to the rising inflation. Many essential food items are experiencing upward price pressure amid ongoing inflationary trends.

item.title: Karnataka targets Rs 7.5 lakh crore investments, 20 lakh jobs by 2030; to host Global Investors Meet in April
item.description: The targets have been set under the state's Industrial Policy 2025-30, with Karnataka seeking investments in sectors such as semiconductors, aerospace, artificial intelligence, clean energy, life sciences and electric mobility.

item.title: Desire within US, India to conclude trade deal by G20: ex-US diplomat
item.description: Negotiations for a phase one trade agreement between the US and India are ongoing and complex. Both countries express a desire to conclude the deal by the upcoming G20 Summit in Florida. Former diplomat Nisha Biswal indicated that significant issues remain, particularly concerning India's comparative advantages. India's Commerce Minister Piyush Goyal stated that the country expects one of the best trade deals with the US.

item.title: Uneven monsoons, El Nino pose upside risks to inflation; another RBI hike possible: Report
item.description: Uneven monsoons and the possibility of El Nino conditions could pose upside risks to food inflation in FY27, keeping the Reserve Bank of India (RBI) open to another interest rate hike despite expectations of gradual moderation in overall price pressures, according to a report by Nuvama Institutional Equities.

item.title: NHC Foods reports 333% quarterly rise in total income to Rs 451.32 crore and over 16-fold jump in profit
item.description: For the first half of FY27, NHC Foods posted total income of Rs 821.45 crore, an increase of 282 per cent from Rs 214.68 crore a year earlier. Profit rose nearly 13-fold to Rs 38.68 crore, compared with Rs 3.01 crore in the year-ago period.

item.title: India needs to create high-quality jobs, increase productivity growth: IMF
item.description: The International Monetary Fund has upgraded India's potential growth to 6.8 percent, citing favorable demographics and a growing economy. Higher productivity growth and stronger private investment are essential to realize this potential. Faster creation of high-quality jobs is also crucial for sustainable economic development. The IMF continues to view India as a key growth engine for the global economy.

item.title: Retail inflation may remain above 6 pc for next few months; economists see possibility of rate hikes
item.description: Mumbai's consumer price index-based retail inflation is projected to remain above 6 percent in upcoming months. This rise is attributed to increasing food prices, an adverse base effect, and commodity price impacts. Economists predict that retail inflation will average 6.2 percent in the October-December quarter of FY27. Heightened food prices and weather-related risks pose ongoing challenges for crop production.

item.title: SBI economists halve December RBI rate hike forecast to 25 bps on easing rupee pressure, foreign inflows
item.description: State Bank of India has revised its estimate for the upcoming Reserve Bank of India rate hike. The new projection suggests a 0.25 percent increase instead of a previously expected 0.50 percent. This adjustment follows improvements in external conditions and a revival in foreign fund inflows. Analysts note that inflation is projected to remain above 6 percent in November before easing.

item.title: India will have one of the 'best' trade deals with the US: Comerce Minister Piyush Goyal
item.description: Commerce and Industry Minister Piyush Goyal stated that India is close to finalizing a strong trade deal with the US. The framework for the initial phase of the bilateral agreement has been completed. However, recent changes in US tariffs have necessitated further discussions between the two countries. Goyal emphasized that the outcomes of the negotiations will be beneficial for India.

item.title: India's 'achievable' FY27 direct tax target faces a make-or-break second half
item.description: India's budgeted direct tax collection target for this fiscal year is Rs 26.97 lakh crore. Current collections are at approximately 53 percent of this target as of November 10. Experts flag the need for a rise in corporate tax and advance tax collections in upcoming months. Non-corporate tax collections have shown slower growth compared to corporate tax collections during the same period.

item.title: RBI plans curbs on private equity firms controlling stakes in multiple non-bank lenders: Report
item.description: India's central bank is working on new rules to prevent private equity firms from holding controlling stakes in multiple non-bank lenders. The proposal aims to mitigate potential financial risks stemming from global private equity firms' investments. While larger stakes will attract greater scrutiny, smaller investments are encouraged to support growth in the financial sector. Recent data shows significant foreign investment in non-bank lenders, highlighting strong demand for credit.

item.title: Use FTAs to build joint ventures, explore investment opportunities: CII President to industry
item.description: R Mukundan, the CII President, stressed the crucial role of Free Trade Agreements (FTAs) in fostering joint ventures and enhancing investment prospects. He noted India's resilient economic growth, even faced with global challenges like geopolitical tensions and elevated energy prices. The broadened scope of India's FTAs promises to enrich economic interactions and spur advancements in emerging technologies such as AI and biotechnology.

item.title: India's net direct tax collections rise 11.8% to Rs 14.42 lakh crore from April 1 to Nov 10
item.description: India's net direct tax collections recorded an increase of 11.76% to reach Rs 14.42 lakh crore. Gross direct tax collections rose by 14.02%, boosting receipts to Rs 17.50 lakh crore. Corporate tax collections grew by about 17.84%, amounting to Rs 6.32 lakh crore. Non-corporate tax collections saw a rise of 5.30%, increasing to Rs 7.56 lakh crore. Direct tax refunds increased significantly, reaching Rs 3.

item.title: Tea industry groups back panel's proposal for minimum sustainable price as costs outpace prices
item.description: Five tea industry associations have welcomed the government committee's recommendation for a minimum sustainable price for tea. This recommendation aims to address rising production costs that are exceeding the prices received by producers. The proposed benchmark price is linked to wage movements and consumer price indices, which will be reviewed periodically. Producers believe this pricing mechanism will help absorb wage increases and support investment in tea production.

item.title: Govt bans export of unsorted battery waste, scrap
item.description: The government has implemented a ban on the export of unsorted waste and scrap from certain batteries. This ban applies specifically to primary cells, batteries, and electric accumulators lacking hazardous substances. The Directorate General of Foreign Trade issued a notification establishing this prohibition, which is effective immediately. Previous regulations classified these exports as 'Free', but now they are categorized as 'Prohibited'.

item.title: India well on track to achieve $1 trillion exports target for FY27: Piyush Goyal
item.description: Commerce Minister Piyush Goyal said India is on track to achieve its $1 trillion goods and services export target in FY27, having already recorded nearly $480 billion in exports during April-September. He highlighted opportunities from free trade agreements, particularly the proposed India-EU pact, for the automobile and mobility sectors. Goyal urged manufacturers to expand globally, boost competitiveness and leverage international partnerships to drive exports, investment and employment.
